title: Miles Ahead — no articles generated in 24h

annotations.summary: Miles Ahead has published no articles in 24 hours
annotations.description: sum(increase(milesahead_articles_generated_total[24h])) is below 1. Scanning can look perfectly healthy while this fires: in the 2026-08-26 incident raw_articles kept filling for 26 days while every generation failed with 410 Gone, because the provider had retired the generator, the critic and the only fallback. NoData counts as firing on purpose — the counter is a CounterVec, so its series does not exist at all until the first article, which is exactly the state an outage leaves it in.

title: Miles Ahead — AI API failures sustained

annotations.summary: Miles Ahead AI API failures are elevated
annotations.description: More than 30 final AI API failures in 6 hours. This is the earlier, noisier signal — the drought alert is the reliable one. Threshold is set above a whole scan cycle failing (~10-20 topics per 3h cycle) so a single bad cycle does not page, but a persistent condition does. NoData is OK here: no errors recorded is the healthy state.

title: Miles Ahead — enrichment reconciler has stalled

annotations.summary: Enrichment has not completed a pass in over an hour
annotations.description: milesahead_enrichment_last_success_timestamp_seconds has not advanced for more than an hour, against a 15-minute interval. This is the signal milesahead_articles_degraded cannot give: that gauge looks identical whether the reconciler is idle with nothing to do or wedged mid-pass, because a stalled pass simply stops updating it. Check milesahead_enrichment_passes_total{outcome} — a rising "skipped" or "deadline" count means passes are overrunning their interval rather than failing outright. NoData is NOT treated as firing here: unlike the article-drought rule, this metric is a plain Gauge and is exported from process start, so its absence means the app is down, which the service alerts already cover.

annotations.summary: Sign-up confirmation emails are failing to send
annotations.description: Two or more confirmation emails failed to send in the last 6 hours (milesahead_emails_sent_total{kind="confirmation",outcome="failed"}). Readers who sign up see "check your inbox" and get nothing, so they never become subscribers. Each failure is logged as "subscribe: sending the confirmation email failed" (journalctl -u milesahead) with the SMTP error; the usual causes are SMTP settings in /opt/milesahead/config.yaml (mail.smtp) or the provider refusing the sender. The claim is released on failure, so a reader who tries again after the fix gets a link. One failure alone does not fire (a single bad address or a provider hiccup is not an outage), but sign-ups are few, so the window is long: a reader who retries after a failure is enough to fire it. NoData is OK: the series are created at zero on startup, so their absence means the app is down, which the service alerts cover.

annotations.summary: A newsletter send stopped with an error
annotations.description: A newsletter send failed in the last 6 hours (milesahead_emails_sent_total{kind="newsletter",outcome="failed"}). A send stops at the first failure, so this counts at most once per send. Check the logs for "weekly newsletter send failed" or "newsletter send failed": if it reached no one the issue is back to its earlier status and can be sent again from the admin Newsletter page; if it reached some readers it stays marked sent (so nobody gets it twice) and the message says how far it got. milesahead_emails_sent_total{kind="newsletter",outcome="sent"} counts readers reached. NoData is OK: the series are created at zero on startup.
